transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-11
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 54m
Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Ravi (Redwood SE), Nina (Redwood SE), Marta (Galleon Head of ML), Liam (Platform), Yuki (Infra), Tom (Product)

Auto-generated summary (brief): walkthrough of right-sizing batching + TTL strategy; cost model discussed; agreed to sandbox sim.

00:00 Samira (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick intro, I'm Samira, AE on the account and I'll run the agenda. Today Ravi and Nina will walk through the Optimize console and show a few scenarios for batching + session/TTL tuning.
00:12 Marta (Galleon): Thanks, Samira. We're eager, we get big spikes from our retail portal and curious how much we can reduce token cost without hurting p95 latency.
00:25 Ravi (Redwood): Great — we'll start with a small baseline: current numbers you shared — 120 RPS average, peaks to 480 RPS, avg prompt+completion tokens ~340, median seq length ~280. We'll use those to build a cost sim.
00:41 Liam (Galleon): Yeah that's right, those are from the logs. One note — we have a chunk of multi-turn sessions where users keep context.
00:52 Nina (Redwood): Cool, that actually favors session/KV cache approaches. We'll demo two axes: batching (server-side continuous batching) and KV/prefix cache (session prefetch or lookahead). We'll show a sim in the console and a quick spreadsheet with unit economics.
01:10 Tom (Galleon): Real quick — we need the p95 under 300ms for interactive chat, but for some background jobs 500-800ms is fine. So any recommendations should keep that p95 constraint.
01:24 Ravi: Understood. We'll keep the interactive route in the low-latency bucket and show fallback options.

02:05 [screen share starts]
02:20 Ravi: Here's the Optimize console. First pane is the traffic profile loader — we can import your histograms. For the demo we'll use a synthetic trace that matches your peaks.
02:38 Nina: Starting baseline sim: no caching, conservative batch target (max batch size 16, target latency 120ms). Result: unit cost X and p95 ~290ms at 120 RPS, but at peak 480 RPS we see queueing, latency spikes to ~520ms.
03:02 Marta: That aligns with our observed spikes. So what's the first lever?
03:08 Ravi: Batching configuration: increasing max concurrent batch depth reduces GPU token cost per request by improving throughput but increases queuing if not careful. For your traffic the console suggests a sweet spot: max-batch 48 with dynamic time-slicing — this reduces per-token cost ~12-18% at steady state, but at peak you might hit p95 spikes.
03:35 Yuki (Galleon): Spike behavior concerns us. Can we do mixed routing? Keep interactive on smaller batch and background on larger?
03:42 Nina: Exactly — Smart routing policy lets you designate latency-tiered routes. We demo a two-route policy: interactive -> low-batch (8) on dedicated low-latency pool; batch jobs -> high-batch (64) on a cheaper pool. The console sim shows combined cost drop ~22% while interactive p95 stays under 300ms.
04:10 Liam: The split sounds promising. How about session KV cache — does that add savings?
04:18 Ravi: Yes, next we look at the KV/prefix cache. Two modes: session-affinity (keep KV on GPU between requests) and lookahead prefetch (prefill KV from last N tokens when a session is hot). For multi-turn chat, a high prefix hit-rate means you avoid recomputing early layers which are expensive.
04:42 Marta: Are we talking about 1-2 tokens saved or bigger?
04:47 Nina: It depends on prefix length. If you have 200 token warm context and a 50-token reply, prefetching a prefix/KV can save ~150 decoder tokens per request on the heavy layers — that's significant. In our sim with your histogram and 65% prefix reuse rate, cost savings climbed another 18-28%.
05:15 Yuki: What's the memory cost for session KV? We run on mixed GPU sizes and worry about eviction thrash.
05:22 Ravi: Good call. The console's capacity planner estimates KV memory per session by model size + KV size per token. For your mix, 8k-context model with quantization, we'd need ~1.3GB per active session for the largest sessions. But you can set TTL/eviction policies: e.g., keep hot sessions for 5 minutes, LRU eviction for low-activity ones.
05:46 Liam: Can TTL be adaptive? Like longer for high-value users?
05:50 Nina: Yes — we support session priority tags. High-value sessions get longer TTL and reserved KV pool slots in Dedicated. That reduces thrash and improves hit rate for your VIP flows.
06:05 Marta: Ok, show me a few TTL scenarios.
06:09 [console sim: TTL slider adjusted]
06:15 Ravi: Scenario A: short TTL (30s) — hit-rate ~18% in our sim, overall cost reduction ~10% vs baseline, p95 improved slightly. Scenario B: medium TTL (5m) — hit-rate ~62%, cost reduction ~36%, but memory reservation up. Scenario C: long TTL (30m) — hit-rate ~78% but memory units cost grows; we also show diminishing returns after ~10m for your workload.
06:51 Tom: So we should probably try medium TTL first. What's the expected CPU/GPU memory increase in numbers?
06:58 Ravi: For medium TTL, additional steady-state memory ~120GB across the pool for your active session estimate — that's in the planner view. We can offset cost by reducing batch depth on the low-latency pool and moving more to high-batch cheap pool.
07:22 Marta: Any non-obvious tradeoffs? Like are we increasing cold-start latency?
07:27 Nina: Prefetch introduces a little upfront work when a session is created, but after prefetch the subsequent requests are faster. There is also more complex state to manage — we produce audit logs and KV eviction metrics in Console to help debug.
07:45 Liam: Can the console tie those metrics to cost line items per token? We need chargebacks across teams.
07:51 Samira: Yes — Console exposes token-level cost breakdowns and per-route model usage so you can allocate spend per product team. We'll share screenshots.
08:05 Marta: Nice. Now the question — how do we pick batch sizes and TTL together?
08:11 Ravi: There's a combined decision surface. We ran grid sims: varying batch size 8->64 and TTL 30s->30m. The console heatmap shows regions where cost is minimized subject to p95 constraint. For your interactive latency requirement p95<300ms, the heatmap indicates a policy with interactive batch 8 + TTL 5m for sessions yields ~32% cost savings vs baseline while meeting SLOs.
08:40 Tom: Are there quick-rule heuristics we can use without running full sims?
08:44 Nina: Yes — general heuristics: (1) if >40% sessions are multi-turn, favor KV prefetch + ≥2m TTL; (2) keep interactive batch small (<16) and route background traffic to higher batch pools; (3) use adaptive batching (target latency windows) rather than fixed large batches; (4) quantify miss-rate sensitivity: if miss rate under 30% you get most of benefits.
09:10 Marta: What's a miss-rate? How do we measure it?
09:13 Ravi: Miss-rate is % of requests where the prefix cache isn't usable. The console includes a simulator and you can also instrument the runtime with a header that reports cache hit/miss per request — we can surface that in logs.
09:26 Yuki: Ok, let's talk about security and data retention for KV. Our legal requires session data to be ephemeral and encrypted.
09:33 Samira: Understandable. Redwood Private offers customer-managed KMS, HSM integrations and you can set KV TTLs/auto-purge. Audit logs are available for KV access. For hosted we have SOC2 controls and per-customer data separation.
09:50 Marta: Good. Any compliance caveats with long TTLs?
09:53 Nina: You'll want to annotate session types; PII-bearing sessions should be short-lived. We can add middleware to strip PII before KV persistence.
10:05 Liam: Can we do partial KV — keep only embeddings or compressed KV to reduce memory?
10:10 Ravi: There are compression and quantization strategies. You can also choose to materialize only top-k layers or store a hashed compact representation. That reduces memory at cost of hit effectiveness. The Console has a compression slider in the planner.
10:26 Marta: Great, show me an end-to-end simulated policy we could pilot.
10:30 [screen: policy builder]
10:36 Nina: Policy: route interactive to route A (batch target 8, auto-timeout 50ms), route B for background (batch 64), session TTL 5m for standard users, 15m for VIP; KV prefetch enabled for sessions >2 turns; reserved KV pool for VIPs. This yields: projected 34% cost savings, interactive p95 ~270ms, peak stability improved.
11:05 Tom: Those numbers look good. How confident are these sims compared to real runs?
11:10 Ravi: Sim accuracy depends on trace fidelity. If you give us real RPS and seq-length histograms we'll calibrate. Historically sims align within 8-12% of measured cost in pilot runs.
11:23 Marta: Ok. Can you run a small live pilot in our sandbox? A few hundred concurrent sessions, with our model and dataset.
11:29 Samira: Yes absolutely. We'll spin up a sandbox and run the policy. We'll need your traffic dump and a short production-like sample model.
11:38 Liam: We can provide a 7-day sample and a container with the model. Note — we prefer the pilot in our VPC if possible.
11:45 Nina: For pilots in VPC/private, we can do Redwood Private or a VPC-delegated setup. We'll scope options after this call — there are additional steps for network setup.
11:57 Marta: One more point: how do rollbacks work if a TTL change causes problems?
12:01 Ravi: The rollout supports canary percentages and automatic fallback on SLA breaches. You can also force a KV flush to clear session state.
12:12 Tom: Ok good. A quick cost knot question — if we reserve dedicated KV pool for VIPs, is that an additional line item?
12:19 Samira: Yes reserved capacity shows as a committed line item in Dedicated pricing; we can model it in the spreadsheet and show the ROI vs on-demand.
12:28 Marta: Alright let's recap next steps.
12:32 Samira: Recap: Redwood to share sandbox cost model + console link (Samira), run initial sim with your 7-day trace once provided (Ravi), schedule pilot kickoff (Samira + Marta). Action items in notes.
12:46 [call closing pleasantries]
12:55 Marta: Thanks everyone, excited to try the pilot.
13:00 Samira: Thanks all, we'll follow up by email with the spreadsheet and links.

--- End transcript (approx 54 minutes)
notes: Customer concerned about p95 <300ms for interactive chat; agreed medium TTL (~5m) with priority tiers and two-route batching. Sandbox to run in VPC or Redwood Private depending on networking. Compliance: KMS and audit logs available.
